samples.summary: API-key branch of the image read route still skips the minter-membership check, so the new "a key does not outlive its minter's membership" invariant does not hold for the whole /api/v1 surface as the docs now claim
samples.evidence: This delta's whole premise is that an API key is resolved to `apiKey.createdBy` and re-checked against that user's *current* membership (`workspace-scope.guard.ts:38`), and docs/design/rest-api.md:509-513 now states `WorkspaceScopeGuard` "enforces the removal half for the **whole** v1 surface" so that "removing somebody from a workspace revokes the keys they minted". `ApiV1ImageReadController` is on that surface (`@Controller('api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/images')`, image-read.controller.ts:40) but mounts only `OptionalCombinedAuthGuard` (line 41) — not `WorkspaceScopeGuard` — and its own gate short-circuits on `if (user?.isApiKey) { if (user.workspaceId === resolvedWorkspaceId) return; }` (lines 96-97), never touching `assertMember` and never looking at `user.id`. Attack: an owner mints a key, is then removed from the workspace (`WorkspaceService.removeMember`, workspace.service.ts:94). Every mutating/reading v1 route now 403s for that key, but `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images/:imageId` still streams any workspace image blob to the holder of the ex-member's key (image ids are learnable from any document content the key holder captured earlier, or from a share link). The gate reads as covered surface-wide when one read path is not.

samples.summary: Member removal still never revokes ApiKey rows; the new membership check only suspends a key, so re-adding the user silently reactivates every key they ever minted (docs claim removal "revokes" them)
samples.evidence: The delta deliberately substitutes a live membership lookup for key revocation — workspace-scope.guard.ts:14-20 and docs/design/rest-api.md:509-513 say this makes removal "revoke the keys they minted without a key-sweep on the member-removal path". But `removeMember` (workspace.service.ts:94-112) only deletes the `WorkspaceMember` row; `ApiKey.revokedAt` is untouched (no `apiKey` reference anywhere under src/workspace), and `ApiKey` has no relation to `WorkspaceMember` (schema.prisma:209-223, key hangs off `workspaceId` + `createdBy`), so nothing cascades. The keys therefore stay valid rows that authenticate successfully (`ApiKeyService.validateKey` checks only revokedAt/expiresAt, api-key.service.ts:65-93) and are merely denied at the membership gate. If the ex-member is later re-invited — `acceptInvite` re-creates the membership with the invite's role, workspace.service.ts:152-178, and a plain-`member` invite is enough — every previously issued key (including one leaked while the person was gone) starts working again with write scope and member authority (create documents, destructive `PUT .../content`), with no operator action and no visibility. Removal is a suspension, not a revocation; the honest fix is to set `revokedAt` on the removed user's keys for that workspace in `removeMember` (the membership check remains a useful belt-and-braces).

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. ApiV1ImageReadController is on the /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/... surface (image-read.controller.ts:40) but mounts only OptionalCombinedAuthGuard (line 41), not WorkspaceScopeGuard. Its private gate short-circuits for API keys at image-read.controller.ts:96-99 on scope match alone, never calling assertMember and never consulting user.id (= apiKey.createdBy, set at api-key.strategy.ts:22-27). Nothing upstream restores the invariant: OptionalCombinedAuthGuard only dispatches (optional-combined-auth.guard.ts:22-32), and ApiKeyService.validateKey checks only revocation/expiry (api-key.service.ts:65-93). WorkspaceService.removeMember deletes the membership row without sweeping keys (workspace.service.ts:94-112), and assertMember (workspace.service.ts:223-230) is the sole enforcement mechanism used by WorkspaceScopeGuard (workspace-scope.guard.ts:34-38). The route is registered and reachable (api-v1.module.ts:14,58). The docs claim the guard enforces removal for the whole v1 surface (docs/design/rest-api.md:522-525), which is false for this read path — an ex-member's key continues to stream any workspace image blob. In-lane (authorization / stale credential) and blocking at major severity: a gate that reads as surface-wide coverage but has an unguarded read path.

Repo-wide greps show the only apiKey mutations are in api-key.service.ts (revoke :59, lastUsedAt :86) plus a test helper; ApiKeyService is injected only into api-key.controller.ts and api-key.strategy.ts, never into the workspace module, so no indirect revocation hop exists, and there is no cron/sweep job in packages/backend/src. searchedFor: prisma/schema.prisma model ApiKey / model Folder cascade rules
finding.summary: `isApiKey → full workspace authority` now also authorizes destructive folder-tree operations, and nothing re-checks that the key's minting user is still an owner/member; removing a member does not revoke their keys
finding.evidence: `isManager()` short-circuits to `true` for any API-key caller (folders.controller.ts:77), and the same short-circuit gates the new document move (documents.controller.ts:128). The only authority proof is `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` (write scope) plus `WorkspaceScopeGuard`, which compares `user.workspaceId` to the route param and never consults `WorkspaceMember` for key callers (workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-32). `ApiKeyService.validateKey` checks only hash/revoked/expiry (api-key.service.ts:65-92), and `WorkspaceService.removeMember` deletes the `WorkspaceMember` row without touching `ApiKey` (workspace.service.ts:94-112); the schema has no cascade from membership either (schema.prisma:209-223 — ApiKey cascades on Workspace, not on membership). Vector: an owner mints `wfb_…` with `write`, is later removed from the workspace by another owner, and the still-valid key now passes `isManager()` and can `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/folders/:folderId` — deleting the folder and, by `Folder.parent onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:137), every descendant folder — for a workspace they no longer belong to. Pre-existing for `documents.remove`, but this change extends the same assumption to the folder tree, so I am flagging it on the new gate; low confidence because keys are plausibly intended as workspace-owned credentials an owner can revoke.

verdict.reason:
The finding's core factual premise is false in this tree. It claims `isManager()` "short-circuits to `true` for any API-key caller" and that nothing re-checks the minting user's live membership. Reading the code:

1. `folders.controller.ts:76-86` — `isManager()` contains no `isApiKey` branch at all. It takes `Number(req.user.id)`, calls `this.workspaceService.assertMember(folder.workspaceId, userId)` and then `isDocumentManager(member.role, folder.authorID, userId)`. The doc comment at :67-74 explicitly states "An API key is **not** waved through... resolved against their membership *now* rather than at mint time." Both destructive paths route through it: move (`:126`) and delete (`:148`).

2. `api-key.strategy.ts:22-27` — `req.user.id` is `apiKey.createdBy`, i.e. the minting user's id, so `assertMember(workspaceId, userId)` is a live membership lookup on the minter, not on the key.

3. `workspace.service.ts:223-230` — `assertMember` does a live `workspaceMember.findUnique` and throws `ForbiddenException('Not a member of this workspace')` when the row is absent. `removeMember` (`:109-111`) deletes exactly that row, so removal immediately fails this check — no `ApiKey` cascade is needed for the claimed vector.

4. `workspace-scope.guard.ts:34-39` — contrary to the finding's "never consults `WorkspaceMember` for key callers", the guard calls `assertMember(resolvedId, Number(user.id))` unconditionally, *after* the API-key workspace-scope comparison, and the header comment (:14-20) states this is deliberately the mechanism that makes member removal revoke keys. `workspace-scope.guard.spec.ts:44-55` covers exactly the finding's scenario (assertMember rejects → request denied).

5. The same live-membership pattern guards the document move the finding cites as also short-circuited: `documents.controller.ts:128-137` (and `remove` at `:175-179`) call `assertMember` + `isDocumentManager` with no API-key exemption.

So the stated exploit — a removed owner's still-valid `write` key passing `isManager()` and deleting a folder subtree — is blocked twice: once in `WorkspaceScopeGuard` before the handler, and again inside `isManager()`.
